hms.note: the needles are held XOR-masked, so every copy found belongs to the store or its cipher; a live AES-256 cipher keeps its key schedule (round keys 0 and 1 are the key) by necessity

summary.egress: HMS local serving (2000 documents, 20000 queries): 0 open network sockets in every lsof sample and no nettop row (nettop lists only processes with network activity); managed Mem0 and Zep not measurable here (no SDK or key)

encryption_at_rest_overhead_hms.note: RSS difference is the Argon2id key derivation's working memory at open; store bytes differ by 15 B

summary.tamper_reading: HMS surfaces every flip in store.json, format.json and encryption.salt as an error, but a flip in the arena segment (seg_0.bin) is never reported: 163 of 163 plain and 172 of 172 encrypted flips opened without error and served different results (the replay treats a frame that fails its CRC or AES-GCM check as the end of the log and drops what follows); flips in documents.text and indices.json changed nothing the fixed queries return. SQLite reports 431 of 1000 (integrity_check or a DatabaseError) and served 1 flip silently; its remaining flips hit bytes the queries never read.

key_zeroization_linux.note: the passphrase is not retained; the derived AES key sits in 5 heap copies while the core is open (a live cipher needs its schedule; 5 copies means the cipher is cloned) and 6 copies remain after the core is dropped: no zeroize on drop
